 Live .  54,532 viewing 54532 viewing Live page Updated 2 minutes ago Antonelli closing in on title in Mexico but race red flagged after Bottas goes off
 Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Close Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Listen live Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Vertstappen leads Mexico City Grand Prix as Antonelli closes in on world championship
 Race red flagged on lap 46 after Cadillac driver Bottas slams into barriers
 Antonelli will clinch title with ninth place - he is currently running in third ( full permutations here )
 Italian Antonelli, 20, would become youngest world champion in Formula 1 history
 Benson Q&A: Send us your questions 
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna
 Post published at 21:23 GMT 21:23 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 It has been there [tension between the two Ferraris], undeclared. There is clearly a battle going on for influence within the team, between whatever it is, camps, certainly between the drivers. They have had incidents and they have had discussions, Lewis said we don't have a rule about how we engage and it seems to me that it was a feisty move by Charles and he was clear that he was not going to give ground. If it meant that both cars went out, then he was going to take that risk.
 160 67 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:20 GMT 21:20 GMT 
 Charles Leclerc is having a big chug in the Ferrari garage, probably watching the highlights that keep showing him running across the grass during his standoff with team-mate Lewis Hamilton. 
 What will Kimi Antonelli be thinking now? The title is right there, but this red-flag stoppage is adding some unnecessary tension to his impeding championship celebrations. 
 191 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:18 GMT 21:18 GMT 
 Pierre Gasly is in the Alpine garage looking at some data, but the Frenchman has been noted for leaving the pit exit on a red light. 
 84 87 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Pit exit closed published at 21:15 GMT 21:15 GMT 
 Lap 46/71 
 As we wait for the repairs to be completed, Max Verstappen is leading, Charles Leclerc is second and Kimi Antonelli, who pitted just before the crash for Valtteri Bottas, is fourth. 
 Lewis Hamilton is in fourth spot but the seven-time world champion has been unimpressed with how his Mexico City Grand Prix has panned out. 
 342 115 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:14 GMT 21:14 GMT 
 Harry Benjamin 
BBC F1 Commentator in Mexico City 
 Valtteri is out of the car, helmet off, walking away, waves to the fans with the assistance of the medical crew.
 611 20 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Hamilton to Ferrari published at 21:13 GMT 21:13 GMT 
 Hamilton: "We've got big, big problems."
 988 297 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:12 GMT 21:12 GMT 
 Lap 46/71 
 The timing of the red flag has not worked out for Lewis Hamilton, who is back on the team radio to say his side of the garage has got "big, big problems". 
 The cameras are following Charles Leclerc as he makes his way through the garage. Is Hamilton there too? Let's see a showdown while the race is stopped. 
 406 89 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:11 GMT 21:11 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 That is massive relief to see [Valtteri Bottas] get out though because he took a while to get out.
 506 28 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:11 GMT 21:11 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 That slow stop has cost Hamilton, because he has dropped in behind Antonelli by a fraction of a second, had he made that two and half second pit stop, he would have emerged in third again, without losing position and he would have run until the end on a soft set of tyres. 
 173 294 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Session stopped published at 21:09 GMT 21:09 GMT 
 Lap 46/71 
 That was a heavy shunt for Valtteri Bottas at Turn One, but the Finn has now climbed out of the car to the delight of the Mexican crowd. It looks like it was suspension failure on the Cadillac that sent Bottas slamming into the barrier. 
 251 125 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Mercedes to Antonelli published at 21:09 GMT 21:09 GMT 
 Engineer: "Safety car."
 Antonelli: "Ah **** mate!"
 196 61 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Safety car published at 21:07 GMT 21:07 GMT 
 Lap 45/71 
 Max Verstappen leads from Charles Leclerc, but Lewis Hamilton has managed to dive in and make a pit stop under the safety car. 
 The medical car has come out and the red flag is shown. Valtteri Bottas seems OK as the marshals arrive on the scene to help the stricken Cadillac driver. 
 351 81 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Bottas goes off published at 21:05 GMT 21:05 GMT 
 Lap 44/71 
 Kimi Antonelli pits - it's a bit slow - and rejoins the action in fourth place on a set of medium tyres. 
 But there's a yellow flag, and it's Valtteri Bottas who has gone off in the Cadillac! 
 113 169 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Leclerc to Ferrari published at 21:05 GMT 21:05 GMT 
 Leclerc: "The car is very difficult to drive."
 Engineer: "Yeah, the wake and also the medium is a worse tyre."
 233 53 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:04 GMT 21:04 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Kimi Antonelli is the only man on the track who is still on the tyres he started on. That's 41 laps on the set of soft tyres, way beyond what Pirelli's predictions looked like and yes he is losing around six tenths of a lap to Max Verstappen chasing him down from behind.
 174 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:04 GMT 21:04 GMT 
 Lap 43/71 
 Charles Leclerc tells his pit wall the car is really hard to drive as he stays in the final podium place in this place. 
 Mercedes are warming up to get Kimi Antonelli in for a pit stop. The Italian is almost there for the 2026 drivers' title. 
 208 45 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:02 GMT 21:02 GMT 
 Lap 42/71 
 Isack Hadjar makes a second stop for Red Bull but the Frenchman is currently out of the points in P15. 
 Lewis Hamilton is still the fastest man in Mexico City, but he's trailing Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc for the podium places. 
 189 90 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 21:01 GMT 21:01 GMT 
 Lap 41/71 
 Oliver Bearman is one of handful of drivers yet to pit, but now the Haas man heads in - and almost ends up in a bit of bother. He manages to slow down his car before he picks up a penalty, and gets back on track in P14. 
 88 31 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris heads in to pit published at 20:59 GMT 20:59 GMT 
 Lap 40/71 
 Image source, Getty Images Lando Norris makes his way, but he just goes a bit too far in front of his crew, making it a slower stop than usual. The reigning world champion rejoins the track in fifth place, just ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri. 
 128 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:58 GMT 20:58 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Just thinking about Ferrari's options here. Lewis Hamilton is very quick, Charles Leclerc is now very frustrated, stuck behind Max Verstappen after the penalty that dropped him back after the pit stops, he is now in that situation where he now can't move forward, if he carries on to the chequered flag, it is likely to finish this way.
